name: StrangeQ
workload: Durable, publisher-confirmed AMQP 0.9.1 queues with 1 KB (and one 64 KB) message bodies, 1/10/30 concurrent pub-con pairs, 20-second runs, consumer prefetch 100, manual acks, driven by the same amqp091-go-based perftest client against both brokers.
claimed_speedup: 1.10x-4.48x higher end-to-end consumed msg/s than RabbitMQ 4.3 across tested workloads (1 pub/1 con: 1.67x; 10 pub/10 con: 4.48x; 30 pub/30 con: 4.41x; 64 KB body: 1.10x)
hardware: Apple Silicon, 16 cores (RabbitMQ run in an OrbStack ARM64-native container; StrangeQ run host-native)
tradeoffs: Only implements a subset of AMQP 0.9.1 (README describes it as AI-assisted, early-stage); RabbitMQ tested containerized (not emulated, but still an extra virtualization layer) while StrangeQ ran host-native, an asymmetry the author acknowledges; durability model (WAL fsync) differs in maturity/track record from RabbitMQ's.
caveats: First-party benchmark on a single Apple Silicon Mac with no specific chip model (e.g. M-series generation) stated, no compiler flags applicable (Go), and an environment asymmetry (container vs host-native) that could inflate StrangeQ's numbers; author explicitly labels this an AI-built project (README: 'I used AI to build StrangeQ'), still very low adoption (5 stars).
found_via: Hacker News: Show HN search tag=show_hn query='message broker' -> 'Show HN: I used AI to build StrangeQ, a RabbitMQ compatible message broker' (https://github.com/maxpert/strangeq)
